function.description: This function is used to create a recommendation model using a given user data and an algorithm type Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_data.description: A data frame of user ratings. Rows represent users, columns represent items, and entries represent user ratings for items

algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

matrix_factorization.description: Optional parameter to indicate whether matrix factorization should be used. Default is False.

Below is a practical, step‑by‑step playbook you can follow to turn your e‑commerce idea into a polished, production‑ready front‑end. I’ll cover the whole pipeline—from design to deployment—so you can pick the parts that fit your team’s skill set and your project’s scale. --- ## 1️⃣ Define the Scope & Gather Requirements | What | Why | Deliverable | |------|-----|-------------| | **Core Features** | Shopping cart, product catalog, search, filters, checkout, user account, reviews, admin panel | Feature list + user stories | | **Target Devices** | Desktop, tablet, mobile | Responsive design spec | | **Performance Goals** | First Contentful Paint < 2 s, Time to Interactive < 5 s | Performance budget | | **Accessibility** | WCAG 2.1 AA | Accessibility checklist | | **SEO** | Product pages indexed | SEO strategy | | **Analytics** | Conversion tracking | Analytics plan | > **Tip:** Use a lightweight project management tool (Trello, Jira, Notion) to keep the backlog visible. --- ## 2️⃣ Choose Your Tech Stack | Category | Options | When to Pick | |----------|---------|--------------| | **Framework** | **React** (Create‑React‑App, Vite, Next.js)
**Vue** (Vite, Nuxt)
**Angular** | React = ecosystem, Vue = simplicity, Angular = opinionated | | **State Management** | **Redux Toolkit** (React)
**Pinia** (Vue)
**NgRx** (Angular) | Use a library if you have complex global state | | **Styling** | **Tailwind CSS** (utility‑first)
**Styled‑Components** (CSS‑in‑JS)
**Bootstrap** (quick prototyping) | Tailwind = fast, maintainable; Bootstrap = rapid | | **Component Library** | **Material‑UI** (React)
**Vuetify** (Vue)
**Angular Material** | For ready‑made UI components | | **Routing** | **React Router**
**Vue Router**
**Angular Router** | Standard | | **Build Tool** | **Vite** (fast dev server)
**Webpack** (customizable) | Vite = modern, fast | | **Testing** | **Jest** + **React Testing Library**
**Cypress** (E2E) | Unit + E2E | | **CI/CD** | **GitHub Actions**
**GitLab CI**
**CircleCI** | Automate builds & deployments | > **Starter Recommendation** > *React + Vite + Tailwind + Redux Toolkit + Jest + Cypress + GitHub Actions* > (You can swap any part for Vue/Nuxt if you prefer.) --- ## 3️⃣ Design & Prototyping 1. **Wireframes** – Sketch low‑fidelity screens (Figma, Sketch, Adobe XD). 2. **High‑Fidelity Mockups** – Add colors, typography, imagery. 3. **Component Library** – Build a reusable component library in Storybook. 4. **Design Tokens** – Centralize colors, spacing, typography in a JSON file. > **Pro Tip:** Keep a “Design System” file so developers can copy‑paste styles without hunting for values. --- ## 4️⃣ Project Skeleton ```bash # Create a new Vite + React project npm create vite@latest my-ecom -- --template react cd my-ecom # Add Tailwind npm i -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer npx tailwindcss init -p # Add Redux Toolkit npm i @reduxjs/toolkit react-redux # Add React Router npm i react-router-dom # Add Jest & React Testing Library npm i -D jest @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom # Add Cypress npm i -D cypress # Add Storybook npx sb init ``` **Folder structure** ``` src/ ├─ assets/ ├─ components/ │ ├─ ui/ # Buttons, cards, modals │ └─ layout/ # Header, Footer, Sidebar ├─ features/ │ ├─ cart/ │ ├─ products/ │ └─ auth/ ├─ hooks/ ├─ pages/ ├─ routes/ ├─ store/ ├─ services/ # API wrappers ├─ utils/ └─ App.jsx ``` --- ## 5️⃣ Build Core Features ### 5.1 Product Catalog ```tsx // src/features/products/ProductList.tsx import { useEffect } from 'react'; import { useDispatch, useSelector } from 'react-redux'; import { fetchProducts } from './productsSlice'; export const ProductList = () => { const dispatch = useDispatch(); const { items, status } = useSelector(state => state.products); useEffect(() => { if (status === 'idle') dispatch(fetchProducts()); }, [dispatch, status]); if (status === 'loading') return ; if (status === 'failed') return ; return (
{items.map(p => ( ))}
); }; ``` ### 5.2 Shopping Cart ```ts // src/features/cart/cartSlice.ts import { createSlice, createAsyncThunk } from '@reduxjs/toolkit'; import { addToCartAPI } from '../../services/cartService'; export const addToCart = createAsyncThunk( 'cart/add', async ({ productId, quantity }) => { const response = await addToCartAPI(productId, quantity); return response.data; } ); const cartSlice = createSlice({ name: 'cart', initialState: { items: [], total: 0 }, reducers: {}, extraReducers: builder => { builder.addCase(addToCart.fulfilled, (state, action) => { state.items.push(action.payload); state.total += action.payload.price * action.payload.quantity; }); }, }); export default cartSlice.reducer; ``` ### 5.3 Checkout Flow 1. **Address Form** – Validate with Yup. 2. **Payment Integration** – Stripe Elements or PayPal SDK. 3. **Order Confirmation** – Show order summary, send email via backend webhook. ### 5.4 User Authentication - **Auth0** or **Firebase Auth** for quick setup. - Store JWT in `localStorage` or `httpOnly` cookie. - Protect routes with a `RequireAuth` wrapper. --- ## 6️⃣ Performance & SEO | Technique | How | |-----------|-----| | **Code Splitting** | `React.lazy` + `Suspense` for route‑based chunks. | | **Image Optimization** | Use `next/image` (Next.js) or `vite-imagetools`. | | **Lazy Load** | `loading="lazy"` on `` tags. | | **SSR / SSG** | Next.js `getStaticProps` for product pages. | | **Meta Tags** | `react-helmet` or Next.js ``. | | **Critical CSS** | Extract with `critical` plugin. | | **Bundle Analysis** | `webpack-bundle-analyzer` or `vite-plugin-inspect`. | --- ## 7️⃣ Accessibility | Check | Tool | |-------|------| | **WCAG 2.1 AA** | axe-core, Lighthouse | | **Keyboard Navigation** | Tab order, focus ring | | **ARIA Labels** | `aria-label`, `role` | | **Color Contrast** | Contrast checker | > **Rule of thumb:** Every interactive element must be reachable via keyboard and screen reader. --- ## 8️⃣ Testing Strategy | Layer | Tool | Example | |-------|------|---------| | **Unit** | Jest + React Testing Library | Test component rendering | | **Integration** | React Testing Library + MSW | Test API calls | | **E2E** | Cypress | Checkout flow | | **Visual Regression** | Percy or Chromatic | Detect UI drift | ```bash # Run unit tests npm test # Run Cypress npx cypress open ``` --- ## 9️⃣ Continuous Integration / Deployment 1. **CI** – GitHub Actions workflow that runs tests, lints, builds. 2. **CD** – Deploy to Vercel, Netlify, or Cloudflare Pages. 3. **Environment Variables** – Store API keys in secrets. 4. **Canary Releases** – Deploy to a staging branch first. ```yaml # .github/workflows/deploy.yml name: Deploy on: push: branches: [main] jobs: build-deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - uses: actions/setup-node@v3 with: node-version: '20' - run: npm ci - run: npm run build - uses: vercel/action@v1 with: vercel-token: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }} vercel-org-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }} vercel-project-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID }} ``` --- ## 🔗 Useful Resources | Topic | Link | |-------|------| | **React + Vite Starter** | https://vitejs.dev/guide/#scaffolding-your-first-vite-project | | **Tailwind CSS Docs** | https://tailwindcss.com/docs | | **Redux Toolkit** | https://redux-toolkit.js.org/ | | **Storybook** | https://storybook.js.org/ | | **Stripe Checkout** | https://stripe.com/docs/payments/checkout | | **Accessibility Checklist** | https://deque.com/blog/wcag-21-checklist | | **Performance Budget** | https://web.dev/performance-budget/ | --- ## 📌 Quick Checklist Before Launch - [ ] All core features implemented - [ ] Responsive design passes on all breakpoints - [ ] Accessibility audit passes (WCAG 2.1 AA) - [ ] Performance budget met (Lighthouse scores) - [ ] Unit + E2E tests passing - [ ] CI/CD pipeline running - [ ] Analytics & error monitoring set up - [ ] SEO meta tags & structured data added --- ### Final Thought Building a front‑end for an e‑commerce site is a marathon, not a sprint. Start small—get a minimal viable product (MVP) running, then iterate. Use the tools above to keep the codebase clean, the team productive, and the customers happy. Happy coding! 🚀
